text: Why can a 27-feature NVAR match a 500-neuron ESN on Lorenz prediction?
choices: Because the ESN's 500 neurons are mostly dead and contribute nothing
Because NVAR uses double precision while the ESN uses single precision
Because the Lorenz dynamics are low-dimensional with quadratic nonlinearities, so degree-2 monomials of recent inputs capture the one-step map almost exactly
Because NVAR is trained for many more epochs than the ESN
explanation: Lorenz lives on a low-dimensional attractor (fractal dim ≈ 2.05) and its ODE has quadratic terms (xy, xz); at small Δt the one-step map is nearly a degree-2 polynomial, which NVAR's monomials represent directly. The ESN must approximate the same structure with many random projections. Precision (option 1) and epochs (option 3, ridge is a one-shot solve) are irrelevant; option 0 overstates — the ESN's features are redundant, not dead.
